onboarding.welcomeDesc:
A simple, privacy-first book tracker.

Your books stay in your own GitHub repository. Nothing is stored on our servers.
onboarding.github: What is a Private GitHub Repository?
onboarding.githubDesc: Bookshelf syncs your book data through GitHub. All your books are stored in your own private repository.
onboarding.tokenDesc:
You'll need a Personal Access Token to authorize Bookshelf.

1. Go to github.com/settings/tokens
2. Click "Generate new token (classic)"
3. Give it a name (e.g., "Bookshelf")
4. Check "repo" scope
5. Click "Generate token"
6. Copy the token here

section.whatIsDesc: A GitHub repository is a storage space for your files. When you mark it as private, only you and people you give access to can see it. Your books will be stored here, synced automatically with Bookshelf.
section.privacyDesc: Your book list is personal data. By keeping it in your own private repository, you control who can see your reading history. No third-party servers store your data – only GitHub, and only because you put it there.
section.yourControlDesc: You own your data. You can download it anytime, delete it, or stop using Bookshelf. Your private repository remains yours forever.

step.createRepoDesc: Go to github.com/new and create a new repository. Give it any name you like (e.g., "bookshelf-books" or "my-reading-list").
step.privateDesc: When creating the repository, select "Private" so only you can access it. Don't add a README or any files yet.
step.initBooksDesc: Add a "books" folder to your repository. You can do this by creating an empty file like "books/.gitkeep" through GitHub's web interface.
step.tokenDesc:
Go to github.com/settings/tokens and create a new token with "repo" scope. This allows Bookshelf to read and write to your repository.

⚠️ The token is shown only once. Copy it immediately after creation and store it somewhere safe — for example, in a password manager.
